title: ENERGY STAR Certified Residential Refrigerators
publisher: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, ENERGY STAR
notes: Dataset p5st-her9; metadata at https://data.energystar.gov/api/views/p5st-her9.json returned name 'ENERGY STAR Certified Residential Refrigerators'. Model rows are recorded in energystar_refrigerators.csv (tasks 2.2 and 2.2.1): every row of the 2026-09-26 Socrata pull, 4,830 rows, of which 4,769 remain after dropping exact repeats of brand, model and kWh (fields brand_name, model_number, annual_energy_use_kwh_yr). In a model number, '*' and '#' each stand for one optional letter or digit (the dataset's 'any of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, version code or blank'); model_normalized keeps them, and the repository matches a query against that pattern. A model listed at more than one kWh keeps every row, so the lookup can see the disagreement and return no figure. Task 2.2.3 (2026-09-26) re-pulled the same 4,830 rows with field product_class and keeps its CFR code (3, 3I, 5I-BI, ...) as a last column, one row per brand, model, kWh and class (4,773 rows): many models are certified twice, without and with an automatic icemaker, and an item's class picks between them.

title: Refrigerator and Freezer Energy Rating Database Search Tool (1949 to July 2021)
publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Weatherization Assistance Program
notes: Downloaded from https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2022-05/refrigerator-freezer-database-search-tool.zip (16.3 MB), the .xlsm search tool. Its hidden sheet RefrigDB_Revised holds 201,797 data rows with brand, model, year, type (R refrigerator, F freezer), configuration, defrost, size in cubic feet and 'Rating', which the tool's own text defines as energy in kWh per year; the tool's separate 'Adjusted Rating' changes it for years in service and door seal ('Good seal = No adjustment'), and only the unadjusted Rating is recorded here. Model rows are recorded in doe_wap_refrigerators.csv.gz (task 2.2.2): 99,716 refrigerator rows, years 1949 to 2021, kept as brand, model_number, model_normalized, year, annual_kwh. Dropped: freezer rows and blank rows (101,302), 769 exact repeats of brand, model, year and kWh, and 10 rows missing a field or with an implausible year or rating. As in the ENERGY STAR data, '*' and '#' in a model number each stand for one optional letter or digit. The DOE page says the database covers models greater than 10 cubic feet and not every model. Check: Maytag MB*2562HE* (2005, 25.1 cu ft) is listed at 505 kWh/year, the figure printed on the older EnergyGuide demo card (demo/cards/label-older-maytag-mb2562.png). The page states no license; it is a U.S. Department of Energy publication.

title: Study of Life Expectancy of Home Components, Table 1: Life Expectancy of Different Products/Items/Materials in the Home
publisher: National Association of Home Builders / Bank of America Home Equity
notes: February 2007 study; the URL is a third-party copy of the PDF, which was read in full text for this row. Table 1, '1. APPLIANCES': 'Refrigerators, Standard 13', 'Refrigerators, Compact 9', 'Freezers 11' (life in years), with the note 'Life expectancy is based on first-owner use.' Table source line: 'Appliance Magazine, Sep 2005 issue, Grainger'. Findings text: 'appliances are often replaced long before they are worn out because changes in styling, technology and consumer preferences make newer products more desirable.' A single point estimate, not a range: refrigerator.json uses 13 for both ends. title: GE Appliance - How to Determine the Age or Manufacture Date
notes: Quoted: 'Our serial numbers begin with two letters, followed by six numbers, with a letter at the end.' The first letter is the month (A January, D February, F March, G April, H May, L June, M July, R August, S September, T October, V November, Z December) and the second letter the year, which 'rotates approximately every 12 years'. Year order from 1980 (G, H, L, M, R, S, T, V, Z, A, D, F) taken from https://www.electrical-forensics.com/MajorAppliances/GeDateCodes.html and checked against GE's own letters for 2015 to 2026 (F, G, H, L, M, R, S, T, V, Z, A, D). Hotpoint, GE Profile, Cafe and Monogram use the same code.

title: Whirlpool Date Codes
publisher: Dr. Ray Franco, PhD, PE (electrical-forensics.com), a third-party reference
notes: Whirlpool serial: 1st letter manufacturing division, 2nd character year code, next two digits week, then the unit number. Letters X and A to J mean 1990 to 1999 and 2020 to 2029; K, L, M, P, R, S, T, U, W, Y mean 2000 to 2009; digits mean the 1970s, 1980s and 2010s. Worked example on the page: Kenmore refrigerator 106.9712611, serial EB1719162, made in week 17 of 1992. The same year table appears on Sears PartsDirect for Kenmore 106 refrigerators (https://www.searspartsdirect.com/diy/article/how-to-find-the-age-of-your-kenmore-refrigerator). A third party's tables, not Whirlpool's own; only the nine-character form is decoded because the page and other references disagree on the ten-character form.

title: Electrolux Date Codes (Frigidaire, Gibson, Kelvinator, White-Westinghouse)
publisher: Dr. Ray Franco, PhD, PE (electrical-forensics.com), a third-party reference
notes: Ten-character serial: 1st manufacturing facility, 2nd product (A refrigerator, B freezer), 3rd last digit of the year, 4th and 5th week, 6th to 10th unit number. Quoted: 'The first digit of the year (the decade) is not in the serial number or model number.' Worked example on the page: LA81503430 is a refrigerator made in week 15 of 1998. A third party's reading, not Frigidaire's own.
